clue.text: One not prepared to strike poet stored weapon here?

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A strike-breaking poet might have kept a sword about him.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAB, a strike-breaker, plus BARD, a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is where a sword or dagger is kept when not in use.

clue.text: Nervous about boy's help

indicators.note: about means wrapped around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: chary means wary or nervously cautious
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A nervous person worries about a boy's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help' looks like what the boy wants, but it is the definition: the British 'daily help' who cleans.
explanation.definitionFit: Help is an old British term for domestic staff, and a cleaning woman is such a helper.

clue.text: Astonishing, and inspiring?

definitions.meaning: amazing, enough to leave one gasping
inspiration is literally drawing air into the lungs

explanation.surface: Something both amazing and uplifting.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means stunning, and literally describes drawing air in, which is what inspiration means.

clue.text: Little woman accepting the wrong stone, a gem

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in the novel Little Women

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the word beside it are put out of order

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A small woman takes the wrong stone when choosing a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes ETH, which 'accepting' puts inside AMY. A stone is a British unit of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a violet quartz used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Girl dressed up to get a husband

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: robed means dressed in robes

explanation.surface: A young woman puts on her finery to win a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Deborah is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Mushroom offered by a sound London club

indicators.note: sound tells us the club's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: the Garrick is a gentlemen's club in London

explanation.surface: A London club serves mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaric is any gill fungus, such as the fly agaric toadstool.

clue.text: So-called playwright's determination

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare is commonly called by his first name
strength of purpose, as in willpower

explanation.surface: The supposed playwright showed great resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve or volition, and the familiar name of Shakespeare.

clue.text: Took advantage of English teacher's initial tolerance

parts.note: play is give or slack, a tolerance in machinery; 'initial' marks it as the first piece
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An English teacher's early leniency is exploited.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To play on a weakness is to exploit it.

clue.text: Take advantage with high ground in battle

parts.note: to have the edge is to hold an advantage
a hill is high ground

explanation.surface: An army seizes the high ground to gain an advantage in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgehill (1642) was the first major battle of the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgehill names the opening pitched battle of the English Civil War.

clue.text: Dead on time? No

definitions.meaning: the ... so-and-so is someone who has died
not punctual, arriving after the due hour

explanation.surface: A dead man is asked whether he arrived punctually, and the answer is no.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deceased and tardy, after the expected hour.

clue.text: Sportingly, one may be slow to give another view

definitions.text: Sportingly, one may be slow to give another view

parts.words: Sportingly, one may be slow to give another view
parts.note: in televised sport, a moment is shown again, often in slow motion, so viewers see it once more

explanation.surface: A sporting person might be slow to offer a second opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Television sport repeats key moments, often slowed, giving viewers a second look.

clue.text: Minimal amount to risk over enterprise, maybe

parts.note: P is a penny, the smallest of sums

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to dare is to risk
a venture is a business enterprise

explanation.surface: A tiny stake is gambled on a business, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an archaic word for perhaps.

clue.text: A yacht-repaired in China

indicators.note: a repaired boat has been put back together, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A yacht is fixed up in a Chinese port.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is the old, poetic name for China.

clue.text: Ill-fated person in dock right to be imprisoned

indicators.note: to be imprisoned is to be shut inside, so one piece is shut within the other

parts.note: the accused is the person standing in the dock at a trial

explanation.surface: An unlucky defendant in court has the right to be locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means doomed or under a curse, hence ill-fated.

clue.text: Full house of kings and queens?

definitions.text: Full house of kings and queens?

parts.words: Full house of kings and queens?
parts.note: a full house is a poker hand, but here a royal house is a line of hereditary rulers

explanation.surface: A poker player holds a full house of kings and queens.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal house is a succession of monarchs from one family, which a ruling line of kings and queens forms.

clue.text: Order reduction in punishment of legion

definitions.text: Order reduction in punishment of legion

parts.words: Order reduction in punishment of legion
parts.note: a Roman punishment killed one soldier in ten from a mutinous legion

explanation.surface: A commander orders a cut as a punishment for his legion.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill one in ten was the Roman penalty for a rebellious unit, later widened to severe reduction.

clue.text: God, clearly not immortal, showing no emotion

parts.note: anything that has died is plainly not immortal
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A god turns out not to be immortal after all, and his face shows nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'Pan, who is dead'; Plutarch records the cry 'Great Pan is dead', so the god is fairly called mortal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face or delivery is expressionless, giving nothing away.

clue.text: Insolent in attitude, going up to trade centre

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters run bottom to top, backwards
in places one word inside another

parts.note: tone is attitude or manner
pert means cheeky or insolent

explanation.surface: Someone with a cheeky manner rises to run a trade centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' builds TOPERTNE and 'going up' reverses it, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a port or depot where goods are imported and re-exported.

clue.text: .Parts of insects girl held up by stake

indicators.note: held means enclosed, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the word to read bottom to top

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is being held up at stake by insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' makes ENNA, which 'held' puts inside the poker stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Antennae are the feelers on an insect's head.

clue.text: Country where I arrive once more?

parts.note: to reland is to come down again, arriving a second time

explanation.surface: A traveller names the nation where they come back time and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation in western Europe.

clue.text: Container used by American is terracotta

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An American uses a terracotta pot as a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a small lidded tin or box for storing things.

clue.text: Fiddle about, not starting difficult task

indicators.note: not starting says the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a stinker is a nasty, difficult job

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles around and fails to begin a hard job.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker is to fiddle with or meddle aimlessly.

clue.text: Hear about bother in agreement

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a judge will hear, or try, a case in court
to eat someone is to bother them, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Someone is told about a nuisance in some deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is the judge's sense: to hear a case is to try it.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

clue.text: One may fall from a little swing

definitions.text: One may fall from a little swing

parts.words: One may fall from a little swing
parts.note: in elections, a swing is the shift of votes between parties; a closely held constituency is lost with only a small shift

explanation.surface: A child might tumble off a small swing.
explanation.walkthrough: A swing in British elections is the percentage shift in votes from one party to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency held by a narrow majority changes hands on only a small shift in votes.

clue.text: Goalkeeper's last to support attack

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: aid is support or help

explanation.surface: The goalkeeper is the last line of defence against an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden attack.

clue.text: Reportedly makes pots

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: to make money is to earn it, so makes means earns

explanation.surface: A potter is said to produce pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, EARNS and URNS sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are large vases or pots, often for ashes or tea.

clue.text: Answer's twice provided by this clue

definitions.text: Answer's twice provided by this clue

parts.words: Answer's twice provided by this clue
parts.note: this clue is numbered 26, and that number is double the answer

explanation.surface: The clue claims to give its own solution twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Twice the number thirteen is twenty-six, the very number of this clue.

clue.text: Told tree can provide what's needed by this bird

indicators.note: the letters of these words can be rearranged to provide something new

explanation.surface: A tree is said to supply what a bird needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The dotterel is a small plover of moors and mountains.
